context.guidance: Store Authentication Secrets with a current, salted, deliberately slow password hashing function, never with a plain or fast unsalted digest. Re-hash each existing record with the new function the next time the Data Principal authenticates. Rule 6(1)(a) requires protection of the Personal Data these secrets guard, and a weak hash removes that protection once the store is read.

value.fix: Replace the fast keyed HMAC on the security answer with a salted, deliberately slow password hash. Use Argon2id (preferred) or bcrypt/scrypt with a per-record random salt and cost parameters set to current OWASP guidance, for example Argon2id with m=19 MiB, t=2, p=1. Apply the normalization you already rely on (trim, lowercase) before hashing. Store the algorithm identifier and parameters with the hash so they can be upgraded later. Keep the existing HMAC value only as a migration source: on the Data Principal's next successful authentication, verify the answer against the legacy HMAC, then immediately re-hash the plaintext answer with the new function and overwrite the stored value. Mark records as migrated, and remove the legacy HMAC path and any HMAC key from the codebase once all records have been migrated or after a defined cutoff. Use a constant-time comparison for verification and do not log the answer or either hash. This addresses SEC-04 and supports the Rule 6(1)(a) protection of the Personal Data the secret guards.
